questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Friends had been there and told me it was a great place to be on exchange - both the academia and the social life

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Bologna is an amazing city, people are nice, the food is awesome, it is easy to visit other italian cities from bologna. The universty is beautiful and most of my courses were interesting and had a great learning outcome

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was easy

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: An e-mail

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: It was OK, it could have been nice to be offered a kind of "mentor" from Italy, to practice the language, learn about the city, meet italians, but otherwise everything else was fine

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I took over an apartment from some friends who were echange students on the spring semester, so it was very easy! But it was very difficult for others, so one advise is to ask people who have been on exhange he same place as you, and ask them for advices

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It's fine, I'm not sure it is possible to live on campus in Bologna

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Found the descriptions of courses at their online portal, and then at a "intra-net", I could choose with couses i would like to enrol at. It was possible to choose more than 30 ETCS points in the beginning, so one could try different courses before choosign the final courses, which was nice

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Yes at the website, and you could get in contact with some students advisors by e-mail or a online meeting

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It was fine, a pitty that many of the courses i wanted were schedueled at the same time

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Read carefully the description and remember that the first or two weeks you can try out different courses before your final desicion

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Overall the level was medium

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Same - lectures, student presentations, guest lectures

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Global development and climate change, Urban studies and cliamte change, Sociology of international migration and History of Italian material culture

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Global development and Climate change was an interesting course, and Raya (the professor) is super cool! I learned a lot, and there were group work which was a nice way to get to learn other students. Sociology of international migration was also a very interesting course! Very interesting lectures and theories. You are going to work with both quantitave and qualitative methods, which is nice and do group work. But it is a course with a big work load, (5 eassays during the semester, one quantitative project, one presentation and one qualitative project) but it was ok, and the learning outcome was really great!

questions.answer: I bought a bicycle - it is not nessecary, but I was really happy that i bought it. And also i spend lot of money on restaurants and going out and trips in the weekends, but one day tours and all weekend tours.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food and drinks are cheap at restaurants

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: no

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: You can join all kind of sports, but it requeries a health check, you can do it through the university, but it can be a long proces and sport is more expensive in Bologna than DK

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Sport, but it is very expensive, and there are beautiful parks for a run. And then ESN did a lot of events, but i didn't attend in any

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Hiking in the dolomites or Bologn hills, Rome, Milan, Florence, Parma, Modena, Venice, Ravenna, the five cities, you can go easily to a lot of italian cities with the fast and cheap train. But Bologna also have a lot to offer - if you like to go out there are lots of clubs and bars, if you like second hand shopping there a many great shops and markets in the weekend, Le Serre in Magherita Jardin was one of my favourte hangout spots for a coffee in sun in the weekends!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Talk with people in your class, when there is group work, choose to be in a group with people you don't know beforehand, go to a sport, talk with people when you are at bars, check events on the weekends e.g. second hand markets or food markets or other events

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: nothing

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Aperetivo!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: The systems are in general more slow and confusing than the danish ones.. so be patient, and it is general better to talk with adminsitration people on the phone or in person than emailing them.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: no

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Experienzing bologna, meeting the italian culture, having  a break from the everydaylife back home

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: nothing

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: no

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
